cells.tense: You are standing in a complete thing, and you can let it go.
cells.act: let yourself be reached by what they are carrying
cells.ask: Next time someone tells you something hard, let it reach you before you sort it — still yourself, just moved.
cells.core:
You can see the shape of something whole — what it is now, not just what it could become — and still stay open to it. That's the difference between finishing and shutting. At the end of a thing you have more than a clear view; you have permission to let it go.

When people bring you what they're carrying, you don't have to fix it. Let it touch you. Not for long, not all day — just long enough that your own answer comes from outside your own head. Staying close without merging is still staying close. The thing you're finishing gets to be finished, and you still get to feel what it did to you.
cells.sheetLine: You can know the whole and still be changed by it.
cells.place: the closing edge of a thing, where the end is also the start

cells.tense: You are watching the end of things before they arrive, and you are judging the version you imagine.
cells.act: decide from what is here now, not from habit
cells.ask: Before you name someone's whole pattern, choose what you can actually observe right now — and decide only from that.
cells.core:
When you could be taking in what's actually there, you're already sending it to the end — what it means, how it fails, who's responsible. The read comes first. The verdict follows fast and feels like the read. From inside it feels clear; from outside, the person across from you has become a case.

Recognising a whole isn't supposed to be finished. Catch the moment you'd push past what's here into a larger frame — and pick what you can genuinely observe now. Decide from that alone. You don't have to stop seeing whole; you just have to stop knowing, for a minute, before the read is done.
cells.sheetLine: You see the end before the middle is through.
cells.place: the closing edge of a thing, where the end is also the start

cells.tense: You were standing at the door of a thing that was already yours, and you couldn't see it.
cells.act: start over as if for the first time
cells.ask: Take something you've carried a long time. Look at it as if you had just arrived — without the story it has.
cells.core:
This one comes from a place of no recognition at all. When you were supposed to see the whole — what you know, what you've done, what you've made — nothing appeared. What other people see in you has not been available to you. You may have found the door in something older, and there may be nothing here to call by its name.

Start over with something close by, as if for the first time. Look at it without the years already attached to it. You don't need a plan. You don't need progress. Let it be new because you're looking at it new. What comes back comes the way it went — quietly, and for the first time.

cells.tense: You are doing the recognising already, and the one who recognises is missing.
cells.act: give back what is owed, and take what is yours
cells.ask: Think of a read you gave away this week — the whole picture, handed off with no credit. Take that one back as yours.
cells.core:
Here's a thing about you: you can read a situation fully, and by the time you've done it, the read feels like what anyone would have noticed. So what you recognised goes into the room and the one who recognised stays outside it — patient, clear, and not counted. You've been the hands for other people's sight, and the sight was yours.

Say it once to yourself: a read you have, whole, right now. Not a theory, not an announcement — just what you can see, held as yours. You're allowed to know what you know before anyone asks for it. The exchange comes back into balance when the one who sees is counted among the ones who see.
cells.sheetLine: The whole you see has had no one standing behind it.

The sentence that serves me is treating the verdict as certainty about the world rather than what it actually is: seeing, going rigid.
